name: Cessna 350/400 Corvalis
summary: Composite four-seat low-wing from Columbia Aircraft, later Cessna, descended from the Lancair ES; it is among the fastest fixed-gear piston singles.

wings: Smooth composite wing with a long, tapered planform
engines: Single flat-six in a sleek, tapered cowl
fuselage: Sleek composite fuselage with a low, wide-cabin profile
Fixed tricycle gear with streamlined fairings

tellTales: Slippery low-wing with fixed gear in streamlined fairings
Low, wide, sleek cabin with a swept tail
Long, tapered nose with a constant-speed prop

confusedWith.howToTell: The Corvalis has no parachute hatch behind the cabin and a smoother, more sloping windshield; the SR series shows its CAPS cover on the rear deck.
The Corvalis has a conventional tail and a wide closed cabin; the DA40 has a T-tail and a bubble canopy.
The Corvalis is a low-wing with fixed gear in fairings; the P2010 is a high-wing.
The Corvalis is a wide composite aircraft with a swept tail; the M20 has a narrow cabin and a forward-swept fin.
